answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to bond collateral in escrow: when k coordinated identities equivocate on correlated claims, their base penalty scales as O(k²), rather than being divided across separate accounts. On detection, forfeiture and asymmetric depreciation apply an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s aggregate capital loss, making coordination costly even when identities appear independent. Splitting stake among mirror nodes, a terrace of lotus validators, does not erase proven shared control.
